samples.summary: `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}">` is still interpolated raw in the very function the diff hardened against attacker-chosen alignment values
samples.evidence: The diff routes `<w:jc w:val>` through the closed `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` map and adds a design-doc table claiming "every value-typed attribute is therefore resolved through a converter that can fail closed" (docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md §3.3). Ten lines above the new lookup, `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` still does `parts.push(`<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>`)` with neither `escapeXmlAttr` nor a converter, guarded only by `if (headingLevel)` — any non-empty string is truthy. `block.headingLevel` is untrusted at the same level `alignment` is: the v1 content PUT validator (`assertValidBlock`, docs-content.controller.ts:360-443) checks `id`/`type`/`style`/`inlines` and never looks at `headingLevel`, so `PUT .../content` with `{blocks:[{id:'b',type:'heading',headingLevel:'1"/><w:jc w:val="right', style:{}, inlines:[]}]}` stores it verbatim. Attacker: a workspace member poisons a shared doc; any other member exporting DOCX gets attacker-chosen OOXML (e.g. field codes) in word/document.xml, header1.xml and footer1.xml. I could not complete the chain end-to-end: both CRDT readers coerce it (`Number(attrs.headingLevel)` at packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:396 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:473), so today the string arrives at the exporter as NaN and the sink emits `HeadingNaN`. The sink is therefore unexploitable-by-accident rather than injection-proof, which is exactly the property the diff set out to establish here — hence low confidence, major impact if a caller ever reaches DocxExporter without the CRDT round-trip (note `putContent` echoes the raw request body back rather than re-reading, docs-content.controller.ts:175).

samples.summary: The extended PUT validator still accepts arbitrary `themes[]` / `masters[]` entry contents, which export sinks dereference with unguarded string ops (stored client-side DoS)
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlidesBody` checks only `Array.isArray` for `themes`/`masters` (line 472-478) and the new walk deliberately covers `layouts` only, on the stated ground that a `Master` holds no `Block`s. That is true, but the entries are still dereferenced unguarded downstream: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:83` does `toSrgbHex(theme.colors[role]).replace(/^#/,'')` and `:89-90` `escapeXmlAttr(theme.fonts.heading)`, and `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/master.ts:31` does `representativeColor(master.background.fill)`. A workspace member can PUT `{... ,"themes":[{"colors":{"text":42}}],"masters":[{}]}` (the deck is stored verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot`, slides-tree.ts:102-105) and every subsequent PPTX export by any collaborator throws a TypeError inside the exporter. Availability-only (no injection: those two sinks escape), and it needs authenticated write access, hence minor.
searchedFor: read assertValidSlidesBody / assertValidLayout / assertValidSlide in docs-content.controller.ts
grep for TextBody occurrences in packages/slides/src/model/element.ts (263/299/391/497) to confirm block coverage
read packages/slides/src/model/master.ts to confirm the 'no Blocks' claim
read packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts and master.ts for unguarded derefs

samples.summary: Inline and cell style *values* are still unvalidated after the diff (only block-style values gained value checks), so a non-string `fontFamily` breaks DOCX export for every collaborator
samples.evidence: The new `assertValidBlockStyle` validates alignment and the five numeric block-style fields, but `inline.style` is only checked to be an object (line 437-441) and `cell.style` likewise (line 410-414). `serializeInlineStyle` in packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:79 assigns `attrs.fontFamily = style.fontFamily` with no `String()` coercion, so a PUT body with `{inlines:[{text:'x',style:{fontFamily:42}}]}` persists a non-string. At export, packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:70 calls `escapeXmlAttr(ascii)` → `value.replace is not a function`, and `isKoreanCapableFamily(42)` is reached first with the same problem. Effect: one authenticated PUT permanently breaks DOCX export of a shared document for all members. Availability only — no injection, since a string that survives is escaped.
searchedFor: grep for String( coercion on fontFamily in the docs codecs

samples.summary: New validator recursion (group children, nested text-body tables) is unbounded on a 25 MB JSON body — cheap stack-overflow 500s
samples.evidence: `assertValidElementData` recurses into `data.children` via `assertValidNestedElement` (line 636-641) and `assertValidSlideBlocks`/`assertValidTextBodyBlocks` recurse through nested table cells, with no depth cap. `bodyParser.json({ limit: JSON_BODY_LIMIT })` allows 25 MB (packages/backend/src/main.ts:20,50), which encodes several hundred thousand nesting levels of `{"type":"group","data":{"children":[...]}}`. An authenticated caller can drive a RangeError (Maximum call stack size exceeded) per request, answered as a 500 rather than a 400. Bounded by the 120 req/min default throttle and it does not crash the process, so minor; I did not confirm whether V8's JSON.parse rejects that depth first, hence low confidence.

samples.summary: Pre-existing, out-of-diff: document-controlled image `src` values are fetched verbatim by the CLI export pipeline (SSRF-shaped)
samples.evidence: `resolveImageUrl` passes through anything with a scheme (line 28) and `createImageFetcher` then `fetch`es it with no host/scheme allowlist (line 48-49). `inline.style.image.src` is attacker-controllable through the endpoint this diff hardens — the PUT validator checks `inline.style` is an object and nothing inside — so a workspace member can plant `src: "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/..."` and a colleague running `wafflebase docs export --format docx|pdf` makes their machine issue that request from inside its network segment, with the response bytes embedded in the produced file. Exfiltration back to the attacker needs the victim to return the file, so impact is limited; reported for completeness since it is the same untrusted-payload surface the diff is tightening.

finding.summary: Untrusted shape `data.kind` is interpolated into the OOXML `prst` attribute with no allowlist and no escaping — reachable from the v1 content PUT API that this change now walks
finding.evidence: `kindToPrst(kind)` returns the model value verbatim (`return kind === 'pentagonArrow' ? 'homePlate' : kind;`) and it is interpolated raw at shape.ts:94 `<a:prstGeom prst="${kindToPrst(data.kind)}">`. `ShapeKind` is a type-only union, so the value is whatever JSON was persisted. Attack: PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did/content with `{"meta":{...},"themes":[],"masters":[],"layouts":[],"slides":[{"id":"s","layoutId":"l","background":{},"notes":[],"elements":[{"id":"e","type":"shape","frame":{},"data":{"kind":"rect\"/><a:evil x=\""}}]}]}`. The new `assertValidElement` (docs-content.controller.ts:504-556) walks exactly this element and validates only `data.text` block styles, so `data.kind` passes; `writeSlidesRoot` (slides-tree.ts:105) stores `slides` verbatim. Any later PPTX export by a viewer emits attacker-chosen XML into ppt/slides/slideN.xml. This is the same sink class the change hardened for `w:jc`/`algn`/`srgbClr val`, missed here.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim is false in this repository. It claims `kindToPrst` returns the model value verbatim (`return kind === 'pentagonArrow' ? 'homePlate' : kind;`) and is interpolated raw at shape.ts:94. In the working tree, shape.ts:24-85 defines `PRST_BY_KIND`, a runtime `Map<ShapeKind,string>` built from an explicit literal allowlist of OOXML preset names, and shape.ts:96-98 implements `kindToPrst` as `return PRST_BY_KIND.get(kind) ?? 'rect';` — an allowlist lookup with a safe fallback. The sink at shape.ts:176 is `<a:prstGeom prst="${escapeXmlAttr(kindToPrst(data.kind))}">`, so the value is BOTH allowlisted and attribute-escaped (escapeXmlAttr at xml.ts:5-12 escapes & < > " '). A `Map` rather than an object literal is used deliberately so prototype keys like `constructor` cannot resolve (documented at shape.ts:15-22, which anticipates the exact v1 content PUT threat model the reviewer describes). shape.test.ts:19-21 asserts the reviewer's own payload `rect"/><a:custGeom><a:pathLst/></a:custGeom><a:x y="` and `constructor` both degrade to `rect`. Because the sink is closed at the sink, the upstream chain (assertValidElement, writeSlidesRoot storing slides verbatim) cannot deliver attacker-chosen XML into ppt/slides/slideN.xml. The verbatim-return code the finding quotes matches the historical draft in docs/tasks/archive/2026/06/20260623-slides-pptx-export-todo.md:715,740, not the shipped implementation. I also checked the only other `prst="${...}"` interpolation (connector.ts:105) to confirm the sink was not merely relocated; it is a connector-geometry path that does not consume ShapeElement.data.kind and is outside this finding's claim.

finding.summary: The new slides-arm block-style validation is bypassable within the same endpoint: `slides[].notes`, `layouts[].placeholders`/`staticElements` and `masters[]` hold the same docs Block/Element shapes and are persisted verbatim with no validation at all
finding.evidence: `assertValidSlide` only does `Array.isArray(s.notes)` (controller.ts:490-494) yet `Slide.notes` is `Block[]` (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:45) — the same docs blocks that reach the same layout engine and are exported through `notesSlideToXml` → `textBodyToXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/slide.ts:205). `assertValidSlidesBody` (controller.ts:452-458) checks only that `themes`/`masters`/`layouts` are arrays, and `writeSlidesRoot` (slides-tree.ts:102-105) assigns all four verbatim; `Layout.placeholders` is `ElementInit[]` carrying text bodies (presentation.ts:56-63). So a caller rejected for `slides[0].elements[0].data.blocks[0].style.alignment` can store the identical value in the same request via `slides[0].notes[0].style.alignment` or `layouts[0].placeholders[0].data.blocks[0].style`. docs/design/rest-api.md advertises the check for 'the docs Blocks inside every text body', so the gate reads as coverage it does not have.

verdict.reason: All three alleged validation holes are closed in the current tree. (1) `assertValidSlide` does not stop at the `Array.isArray(s.notes)` check — docs-content.controller.ts:557 calls `assertValidSlideBlocks(s.notes, `${path}.notes`)`, which at lines 683-720 rejects non-object blocks/styles and runs `assertValidBlockStyle` (line 698) plus recursion into `tableData.rows[].cells[]`, i.e. exactly the same style validation applied to `slides[].elements[].data.blocks[]`. (2) `assertValidSlidesBody` does not stop at the `themes/masters/layouts/slides` array check: lines 493-496 loop every layout into `assertValidLayout`, which walks both `placeholders` and `staticElements` (lines 507-514) via `assertValidNestedElement` (595-600) -> `assertValidElementData` (612-642) -> `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` (664-676) -> `assertValidSlideBlocks`. So `layouts[0].placeholders[0].data.blocks[0].style` is checked. (3) `masters` genuinely carries no Block/Element shapes: `Master` is `{ id, themeId, background, placeholderStyles }` with `placeholderStyles` being scalar `PlaceholderStyle` records (packages/slides/src/model/master.ts:29-34, 36-50), so there is nothing of that shape to validate. The reviewer's cited line numbers (controller.ts:490-494 and 452-458) do not correspond to the code they describe in this tree — 490-492 is the comment explaining why masters needs no walk, and 493-496 is the layout walk itself. Secondarily, the claimed impact (malformed style/geometry values reaching the layout engine) is input hygiene rather than authz/secrets/injection/crypto/SSRF/traversal, so it would fall outside the Security lane even if present.
